## 1. Effect of input parameters on the ForSys land base

The map below was generated using the input parameters provided for the proposed scenario. The layers in the map can be toggled on and off to examine the spatial distribution of the priorities in relation to the lands available to for treatment by ownership and land use type.
  


```{r echo=FALSE}
#suppressWarnings(print(available_plot_leaflet))
htmltools::tagList(available_plot_leaflet)
```



## 2.	Effect of ForSys land base filters on the total area and priority available for treatment. 

The table below contains the effect of land base filters on total area and priority available for treatment. Each row contains the residual area and priority available after implementing the specific filter. When more than one threshold is used, the second threshold is applied after the first one, further filtering the area and priorities.  The Priority data show the amount of the total priority (%) that is in the land base available for treatment after each filter is applied. This is also referred to as PCP in ForSys outputs.   The priority data are also expressed on a per area basis to show how the potential treatment leverage (i.e. priority per acre) is affected by the filters.  Expected fire impacts on priority (% burned per year) is calculated if the user has included burn probability in the input data. Impacts are calculated as the expected area burned x total priority (%).  Expected area burned is calculated from the National FSim burn probability data.  High intensity fire is calculated as the percentage of the area in column Residual area that burns at high intensity (either flame length >= 8 feet or flame length >= 2.5 meters).
  
```{r }

  collapse_rows_df <- function(df, variable){
  group_var <- enquo(variable)
  df %>%
    group_by(!! group_var) %>%
    mutate(groupRow = 1:n()) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(!!quo_name(group_var) := ifelse(groupRow == 1, as.character(!! group_var), "")) %>%
    select(-c(groupRow))
  }
  
  
  
  
area_considered_table%>%
    #collapse_rows_df(Parameter)%>%
    knitr::kable(caption="")
  
  
  
```
